chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad ibn Suheyb who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: There is no problem with looking at the heads of the people of Tihama, the Bedouins, the people of Aswad, and the Uluj, because when they are forbidden, they do not desist. He said: And the insane woman, and the one whose intellect is overcome, and there is no problem with looking at her hair and her body, as long as one does not deliberate that.

key_terms.التِّهَامَةِ: A region in Arabia, often associated with specific tribal characteristics
key_terms.السَّوَادِ: A tribe or group, often contrasted with Bedouins
key_terms.الْعُلُوجِ: A tribe or group, often mentioned alongside Aswad
key_terms.الْمَغْلُوبَةِ عَلَى عَقْلِهَا: The one whose intellect is overcome/weak

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on looking at women's heads and bodies according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling to highlight the practical flexibility in visual modesty, noting that for groups like the Bedouins and Uluj, prohibitions are often ineffective, making a permissive view more pragmatic. The hadith further extends this leniency to women with intellectual disabilities, permitting observation of their hair and body as long as the gaze remains non-lustful and intentional. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of 'ease in the absence of strict prohibition' when dealing with specific social contexts.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad Bin Suheyb who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no problem with looking at the heads of the negligent women, and the Bedouins, and the Nomads, and the Infidels, because when they are forbade, they will not be desisting; and the insane woman, and the one whose intellect is overcome, and there is no problem with looking at her hair, and her body for as long as you do not deliberate to that’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abbad ibn Suhayb who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ’It is not unlawful to look at the heads of the people of al-Tihamah and Arabs who live in black (tents) and al-‘Aluj (faithless uneducated people) because even if they are prohibited they do not listen.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘In the case of insane and those whose reason is defeated (very weak) it is not unlawful to look at their hairs and body as long as it is not an intentional look.’”
